title: Wren and the Alibi
premise: When twin letters arrive at the office of small-town coroner Bram Marchetti — one confessing to a murder no one has reported, the other promising a second death — Bram realizes the victim is a man whose autopsy they signed off as natural causes. As Bram quietly reopens the file, the killer begins feeding them evidence, forcing them to choose between the law that failed and a justice that demands complicity. The trail leads to a decades-old cover-up involving the town's founding families and to Wren Calloway, the letters' author, whose sister was the first victim. In the end, Bram must decide whether to hand Wren over or help her finish what the courts never started — and their choice costs them both the badge and each other.
about_author: Wendell Nystrom spent fifteen years as a rural paramedic before turning to fiction, drawing on the quiet devastations he witnessed in county morgues and kitchen-table vigils. He writes from a farmhouse in upstate New York, where he keeps his late father's coroner's field manual on the nightstand.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Name
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. On an ordinary Monday, two letters arrive: one confessing to killing Daniel Voss, one promising 'the next one by Friday.' The problem: Bram autopsied Voss three weeks ago and ruled it cardiac failure. Rattled but intrigued, Bram pulls the old file and finds a detail that doesn't fit — a needle mark hidden under Voss's collar. The beat is unease: the comfortable certainty of a small-town expert cracking open.

chapters.title: The Grave That Doesn't Add Up
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram exhumation-orders Voss's body against the sheriff's advice and confirms poisoning with a paralytic undetectable on standard screens. Someone with forensic training did this. Meanwhile, a third letter arrives containing a photograph of Bram's own office taken from outside. Emotional beat: isolation — Bram can trust no colleague, and the killer is watching, almost admiring.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, shifting to Wren's at midpoint. Following handwriting analysis to a shuttered bookstore, Bram meets Wren Calloway, who admits to writing the confession — for a murder she says she witnessed twenty years ago, when her sister died the same way. She isn't confessing; she's recruiting. Beat: magnetic suspicion — Bram should arrest her but instead sits down and listens.

chapters.title: What the County Buried First
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback chapters braided into present: Wren recounts her sister Lena's 'accidental' death in 2003, ruled by then-coroner Aldous Pike — Bram's mentor. Present-day Wren shows Bram Pike's old ledgers, purchased at an estate sale, listing payments from the Hollis family. Beat: grief weaponized into purpose; Bram's faith in their own history begins to rot.

chapters.title: Friday Comes Anyway
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Despite the investigation, the killer's promise holds: a second body, councilman Everett Hollis Jr., found staged exactly as the letter predicted — down to details only the case file contains. The killer isn't just watching the case; they're inside it. Sheriff names Wren the prime suspect. Beat: dread and guilt — Bram's curiosity may have armed a murderer.

chapters.title: The File Reads Back
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Comparing the crime scene to the leaked file, Bram finds a deliberate error planted in the staging — a mistake only someone who wanted to be caught would make. The killer wants an audience who understands. A fourth letter reveals the author knows about Bram's meetings with Wren. Beat: paranoia curdling into complicity; Bram hides evidence for the first time.

chapters.title: Aldous Pike's Last Round
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Bram confronts the retired, dementia-shadowed Pike, who alternates between denial and lucid fragments implicating the Hollis patriarch in Lena's death. That night Pike dies — the fifth letter arrives before the body is found. Beat: horror and heartbreak; the past is not merely repeating, it is being executed on schedule.

chapters.title: The Confession Trap
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Realizing the letters predict deaths because Wren's accomplice is someone with file access, Bram sets a trap: falsifies a case entry naming a fake next target. When the killer strikes the decoy location, Bram catches Deputy Cora Lindqvist — Pike's protégée, Lena's childhood friend, and Wren's secret partner. Beat: betrayal inverted — the monster was grieving too.

chapters.title: Justice, Hand-Delivered
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. With Cora caught, Wren goes after the last name on her list: the elder Hollis, dying in hospice and untouchable by any court. She asks Bram — once — to look away. Bram arrives instead, stands between Wren and the bed, and offers her something better: a recorded deathbed confession, extracted by Bram's professional authority. Beat: love against duty resolved sideways — neither surrenders to the other's code.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, epilogue months later. Bram resigns rather than testify cleanly against Wren, whose sentence is lightened by the Hollis recording; Cora takes the weight of the murders. Visiting the cemetery, Bram recites the graves by name — including Lena's, now corrected on paper — and finds a final envelope: blank except for 'Thank you.' Beat: bittersweet peace; justice arrived, but everyone paid.
